claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a high-temperature single BCC phase.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between a composition-dependent thermodynamic driving force for chemical ordering and kinetic diffusion barriers.
Chemical ordering promotes phase decomposition in this alloy.
Kinetic diffusion barriers delay chemical ordering in this alloy.
Rapid quenching can lock in the high-temperature BCC structure and suppress ordering.
Isothermal aging near a transformation threshold allows thermodynamic instability to overcome kinetic diffusion barriers.
The phase transformation is mediated by nanoscale, compositionally distinct ordered precipitates emerging within the BCC matrix.
Lowering temperature increases the free-energy difference favoring chemical ordering.
Lowering temperature increases the free-energy difference favoring phase separation.
Diffusion of Cr, Co, Fe, and Ni is kinetically limited under the relevant transformation conditions.
The balance between ordering driving force and elemental diffusion rates determines ordered-precipitate nucleation and growth.
Samples aged near the threshold temperature will develop nanoscale ordered precipitates.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain the high-temperature BCC structure with minimal chemical ordering.
Ordered-precipitate size and amount will increase with longer aging durations within the effective transition regime.
At temperatures significantly above the threshold, insufficient thermodynamic driving force prevents transformation.
At temperatures well below the threshold, sluggish diffusion can prevent observable ordering on practical timescales.
